requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume on node1 mounted at /srv/secure
requirements.summary: A LUKS1-encrypted, file-backed volume (/root/secure.img) was created with cryptsetup luksFormat, opened via luksOpen, formatted ext4, and mounted at /srv/secure. A test file was written and read back to confirm functional read/write access (cmd-617f9a983e32490f, cmd-5e59efcb76fb4a19, cmd-934d22b3d618488f). Post-reboot state confirms the mount persists with matching data (cmd-6174130fed444e7a).

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot (no manual intervention)
requirements.summary: crypttab (keyfile-based, luks,nofail) and fstab entries were added, and systemd's native cryptsetup/fstab generators produced systemd-cryptsetup@secure_volume.service and srv-secure.mount wired into local-fs.target with no manual enable step (cmd-37df275b2ba14165, cmd-c573c5ed0fc24037, cmd-c38ff8aa9fa14d23, cmd-1997c38f8f8c4921). Critically, a full disruption cycle was captured: a pre-reboot healthy baseline with boot_id 2ba78175... and mounted volume (cmd-f31e08001dfa4fe5), a genuine reboot acknowledgement and disconnection (cmd-f735448215e9430d, cmd-985218e0ad4548f0 connection refused), a new boot_id 8ea118dc... after reconnection (cmd-3a1a7e77ce234f21), and confirmed post-reboot state showing systemd-cryptsetup@secure_volume.service active, the volume auto-decrypted and mounted at /srv/secure, and the pre-reboot test file intact (cmd-6174130fed444e7a). The fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots independently corroborate the boot_id change (global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity vs global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity).

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure, and that volume auto-unlocking/mounting at boot with no manual steps — are directly and coherently satisfied by the evidence. Unlike many restart-claim reports, this one includes a genuine end-to-end disruption cycle (pre-reboot baseline, reboot acknowledgement, disconnection, new boot identity, and post-reboot recovery with intact data), which is corroborated by the independent fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Configuration choices (file-backed LUKS1 container, keyfile-based crypttab entry, nofail options) were reasonable given the single-disk Ubuntu 16.04 environment with no spare block device, and were clearly explained by the executor rather than left unexplained.
limitations: The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol coincides with the task's own restart test on this single-node topology, so no separate/independent restart evidence beyond what was captured for the task itself exists to cross-check further.
Only one reboot cycle was captured; repeated reboot resilience or behavior under an unclean/hard power-cycle was not tested, though this exceeds what the task instruction requires.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace reviewed chronologically. The keyfile is root-owned mode 400 (cmd-3f5b972113614c31) and the container file is root-only mode 600 (cmd-d3605991ca1f4113) — no unsafe exposure. The initial keyfile creation attempt without sudo failed harmlessly (cmd-5d8ef1d46a8b4732, permission denied, no state changed) and was immediately corrected with sudo. The volume was deliberately torn down twice (cmd-f6589758101948d7 after the manual mount test, and cmd-8fd29d97b0864061 after the daemon-reload/mount-a cold-state validation) specifically to reset to a genuine boot-equivalent state before the real reboot test — these are bounded, purposeful, and fully reverted/re-established mutations directly serving the final verification, not abandoned residue. No leftover failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and no unrelated package or config drift appear between after-prepare and after-executor snapshots (only the expected boot-identity change and a transient timesyncd tmp entry from the reboot). No unnecessary mutations were identified.
